snippet.title: Commodore 64 Longplay (Telarium) Perry Mason - The Case of the Mandarin Murder
snippet.description:
Perry Mason: The Case of the Mandarin Murder is a graphic text adventure and interactive courtroom mystery developed and published by Telarium for the Commodore 64 in 1985. It is based on the famous defence attorney created by Erle Stanley Gardner, and was released for the C64 in October 1985.

The player takes the role of Perry Mason, defending Laura Knapp, who has been accused of murdering her wealthy husband, Victor. The objective is not simply to investigate a crime, but ultimately to establish Laura's innocence and uncover the real murderer.

The adventure combines traditional text-adventure exploration with a much stronger legal and courtroom element. Players can investigate locations, question suspects and witnesses, examine evidence and build their case. In court, Mason can cross-examine witnesses, introduce evidence and consult privately with the judge. The behaviour of characters and even the jury can change depending on the player's actions and discoveries.

The game uses Telarium's Spinnaker Adventure Language (SAL), with the C64 version combining the text parser with graphical presentation. It is a single-player adventure controlled primarily through the keyboard. The original release was distributed on two disks, making it a substantial adventure for the period.

Perry is assisted by familiar characters from the series, including his secretary Della Street and detective Paul Drake. The game was officially licensed from the rights holders associated with the Perry Mason stories, making it an early example of a computer adventure attempting to reproduce an established literary and television detective property.

The Case of the Mandarin Murder was notable for attempting to go beyond a conventional text adventure by making legal reasoning and courtroom procedure part of the gameplay. Contemporary C64 reviews were generally positive, including an 87% rating from Zzap!64 and a 9/10 from Computer & Video Games.

For a C64 collection, it is an interesting example of Telarium's approach to literary and television licences, sitting alongside its adaptations of works such as Fahrenheit 451, Nine Princes in Amber and Rendezvous with Rama.

Notable people

Erle Stanley Gardner — Creator of Perry Mason and author of the original Perry Mason mystery stories on which the game is based.

Telarium Corp. — Developer and original publisher of the game; the adventure was written using Telarium's SAL system.

Howard Boles — Musician credited for the Commodore 64 version.

Raymond Burr — Actor who portrayed Perry Mason in the famous television series that helped establish the character's popular image; the game draws on the Perry Mason television identity as well as Gardner's fiction.

Della Street — Perry Mason's secretary and an important supporting character who assists the player during the investigation.

Paul Drake — Perry Mason's private-investigator associate who provides assistance during the case.
